title: Unauthenticated backend health-check endpoint publicly accessible at /api/health
description: https://zakerne.com/api/health returns HTTP 200 with JSON body {"ok":true} and no authentication required, confirming the existence of a live backend API reverse-proxied through Cloudflare under the same domain (distinct from the SPA's client-side catch-all routing, which returns the index.html shell for unmatched paths). This is a minor information-exposure/attack-surface confirmation finding: it validates that a real API host exists at /api/* and responds distinctly from the SPA fallback, which is useful for subsequent web-app testing but is not itself sensitive data.
reproduction_steps: Compare to curl -s -D - https://zakerne.com/api/v1 or other unmapped API paths (which correctly 404 with text/plain), and to arbitrary unmapped paths at the site root (which return the 4250-byte SPA index.html with HTTP 200 - a false-positive trap for naive directory brute-forcing).
impact: Very low impact on its own (no secrets, no version banner, just a liveness boolean). Primarily useful as a map of real backend attack surface for the pentest-web phase: confirms /api/* is a genuine backend route namespace (with proper 404 handling for unmapped sub-paths) as opposed to the SPA's universal catch-all, and that CORS on /api/* does not reflect arbitrary Origin headers (Access-Control-Allow-Origin was not present in a cross-origin OPTIONS preflight test with Origin: https://evil.example.com), which is a positive control.
remediation: No action strictly required; optionally restrict /api/health to internal monitoring / require a shared secret or IP allowlist if the client wants to minimize any automated-scanner attack-surface fingerprinting, though this is standard practice for most SaaS apps and low priority.
